questions.question: What is a dam, and give four reasons why people build dams.
questions.expected_answer: A dam is a wall built across a river to hold back water, which collects in a reservoir. Dams store drinking water, provide water for irrigation, make hydro-electric power, help control floods, and are used for recreation.

questions.question: Describe three ways a dam changes the environment upstream.
questions.expected_answer: Land behind the dam is flooded, drowning farms, riverbanks and buildings, so people must move; plants and animals lose their habitat; the flowing river becomes a still lake; silt settles and slowly fills the dam; and water is lost to evaporation from the wide surface.

questions.question: Describe two changes a dam causes downstream, and one benefit.
questions.expected_answer: Less water flows downstream and floods become smaller and rarer, so wetlands and floodplains can dry out; the water is clear and cold, so riverbanks wear away and less sand reaches the sea; the steady flow helped blackflies to breed; and the wall blocks fish. A benefit is a reliable supply of water for farms and towns, and flood control.
